correctness.rationale: The Fano point–line incidence relation a·p=0 over F2 gives 14 vertices, 21 edges and max-degree-one face criterion. An independent exhaustive face enumeration reproduced 2256 faces with f=(14,91,322,651,728,392,58), the full 1121-pair pivot matching, one zero-cell and thirteen critical five-cells; 10150 directed incidences topologically sorted acyclically, proving the integral wedge. Independently enumerated 168 invertible 3×3 binary matrices and their 168 duality coset permutations; signed Lefschetz traces (13,5,1,1,−1) by preserving element order and all −1 for dual elements imply χ=1+2(fixed Fano points−1), yielding 1⊕2W and a duality-odd unique GL3 invariant line. Integral wedge does not require an F2 homology assumption.

originality.rationale: Prior Heawood ordinary independence, graph matching, perfect-matching and two-matching complexes have different face predicates and homology. Published Deshpande–Singh higher-independence family theorems cover selected complete multipartite, whiskered, cycle and tree families, not the Heawood incidence graph. The assessed novelty is a precise graph-specific Ind_2 integral type and all-336-element character, not defining higher independence itself.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a fundamental highly symmetric cubic girth-six incidence graph, and degree-bounded vertex sets form a canonical nontrivial complex. Exact integral homotopy and representation of all 336 automorphisms give a meaningful topological-symmetry invariant, including a counterintuitive duality-odd invariant line.

final_claim: The complex of vertex subsets inducing Heawood maximum degree at most one has integral homotopy type ∨13 S⁵; as a rational GL3(F2)-module H̃5≅1⊕2W, and the full point–line duality group has zero invariant classes.
limitations: Exact Heawood graph and parameter 2; not a theorem for arbitrary cubic graphs.
Rational module statement does not determine the integral representation lattice.
